_comment: The patcher window's "?" guides. One short, plain guide for every button, tool and setting the window shows, by control key. Each guide is a list of short lines: what it does, how to use it, and what to watch out for. tests/test_how_to_use.py refuses a control without one, and a guide that is too long.

getting_started.title: Getting started
guide: This patcher makes a separate modded copy of your Virtual Families 2 folder. Your original game folder and your original saves are left alone.
1. Pick your vanilla Virtual Families 2 folder (the one holding Virtual Families 2.exe). 2. Tick the patches you want. 3. Click Dry Run, then Enable/Disable Patches.
Vanilla Virtual Families 2 saves work with the modded game. The modded game keeps its saves in its own folder, so use Back Up Saves on the Tools tab before trying a new build.

game_folder.title: Vanilla game folder
guide: The folder of your official Virtual Families 2 install: it holds Virtual Families 2.exe, Images, Sounds, Assets and the game's other program files.
Click Browse and pick it. The patcher checks it looks right before it changes anything.
Leave it empty only when you are re-configuring a modded folder you already made.

manifest.title: Patch manifest
guide: The list of patches this patcher can apply. manifest.json loads by itself when the patcher starts.
Only pick another manifest if someone gave you one.
Load Manifest Settings reads it again and redraws the patch list.

output_folders.title: Modded output folder
guide: Where the modded copy of the game goes. It is made next to your vanilla folder unless you pick another place.
Save modified folders under: the folder the new modded folder is made in. Modded output folder: an exact folder, such as one you made before.
Never pick your vanilla folder as the output folder.

backup_folder.title: Backup folder
guide: Each time you rebuild an existing modded folder, the patcher first saves a complete copy of the old one (about 230 MB).
By default each copy goes in a new dated folder under .vf2_patch_backups. Pick a folder here to put them somewhere else.
The patcher never deletes these copies: delete old ones yourself to free disk space.
These are copies of the game files. Your saves are backed up by Back Up Saves on the Tools tab.

patch_log.title: Patch log
guide: A text record of exactly what a run changed.
Leave it empty for the default place, or Browse to choose a file.
Send it along if you ask for help with a patch problem.

patch_selection.title: Choosing patches
guide: Tick the patches you want. Main Patches are the core fixes, Optional Patches add extra content, and Experimental patches are unfinished (shown in red, and off unless you tick them).
Defaults ticks the recommended set. Enable All ticks everything except Experimental. Disable All clears every tick.
Some patches need another one. Ticking one ticks what it needs, and unticking a needed patch unticks what depends on it.

dry_run.title: Dry Run (Validate Only)
guide: Checks that your game folder and your patch choices work, without writing anything.
Click it before Enable/Disable Patches, especially the first time.
If it reports a problem, nothing was changed; fix what it names and run it again.

apply.title: Enable/Disable Patches
guide: Builds the modded folder from your vanilla game with exactly the patches that are ticked.
Changed your mind later? Tick or untick patches and click it again: the modded folder is rebuilt from vanilla with the new choices.
An existing modded folder is copied to the Backup folder first. You can bring it back with Restore Backup.

restore_backup.title: Restore Backup
guide: Puts back a game-folder copy the patcher made before a rebuild.
Browse to the dated backup folder and click Restore Backup. It is restored into the folder it was taken from, never into your vanilla folder.
Restore log: where to write the record of the restore (optional).
This is for game files. To bring back saved families, use Restore Saves on the Tools tab.

check_updates.title: Check for updates
guide: Opens the patcher's download page in your web browser.
Compare the build number at the top right of this window with the newest one listed there.
Back up your saves before moving to a new build.

back_up_saves.title: Back Up Saves
guide: Copies your family saves into a dated folder inside the save folder: Documents\LDW\<game>\Backups\Backup <date and time>.
It copies the game's save files and the patcher's own files too (the Virtual Families 2 Patcher Data folder, which holds the extra children).
Click it, tick the save folders to copy, click Back Up Selected. If the game is running it is paused for the copy and resumes by itself.
The game saves only when you quit normally, so a backup of a running game holds your families as of the last save.
Every copied file is checked against the original. An older backup is never written over.

restore_saves.title: Restore Saves
guide: Brings back a backup made by Back Up Saves: the whole save folder, or just one family's save slot.
Quit the game first. Pick a backup (newest first), choose the whole folder or one slot, and click Restore.
You are shown exactly which files will be replaced, added or removed, and nothing changes until you say yes.
Your saves as they are now are backed up first as "Backup <date> (before restore)", so a restore can always be undone.
Delete Backup... removes a backup you no longer need.

update_family_logs.title: Family Logs
guide: Writes each family's story beside its save: Family History, Births and Conceptions, Deaths, Events, and Population and Statistics pages.
It runs when the Tools tab opens and when you click Update Family Logs. It never runs while the game is running: quit the game first.
The logs come from comparing the saves the game writes when you quit (and the save before) with the ones logged last time.
Events are dated by the save they first appear in. Something that starts and ends between two saves cannot be seen.
A family logged for the first time gets its past from the family tree, marked "backfilled, no date".
The save does not say why someone left home or what caused a death, so the logs say "left home" and "cause not recorded".
Start Over or a new family starts fresh logs; the old ones move to Save <N>\Backups.

how_to_use.title: How to Use guide
guide: Opens the full guide: every button and tool in this patcher, one short page each.
Pick a topic on the left to read it.
Every "?" button in the window opens the page for the control beside it.
